geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the repetitive radial branching with a more coherent stepped section that can read as inhabitable terrace massing instead of a spiky cap.
Keep the step count restrained so the silhouette reads as a continuous terraced mass rather than arbitrary tiers.
Introduce a mild, legible terrace depth to support the neighborhood-living section without over-fragmenting the form.
Align the step logic with the long axis so the mass reinforces the dominant bar gesture.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the existing courtyard aligned to the program’s required access side and strengthen the public threshold rather than sealing the frontage.
Open the internal void slightly more so the carved space reads as public and not as a residual notch.
Replace the visually repetitive branching/array logic that contributes to the bulky stepped silhouette with a cleaner section operation.
Keep the dominant gesture but make the longitudinal curvature more legible and less like a fragmented tiered cap.
Reduce the bend intensity so the form stays continuous and avoids the over-crushed pyramidal look.
Simplify the bend discretization to improve continuity and reduce visible segmenting.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact mass with a recognizable carved/courtyard gesture, so it has baseline gesture clarity and some precedent resonance. However, the form is still too pyramid-like and visually compressed; the stepped/bent language produces a thick, truncated object rather than a clear neighborhood-living body with an active ground threshold. The blue access edge is not strongly answered by a public void or entry seam in a way that is legible across all views. In section, the mass does not yet communicate a convincing inhabited public edge or terrace logic; the roof/upper silhouette feels more like a sculptural cap than a program-driven section. Because the program brief requires an active street threshold and public void, the current form is only partially program-fit and fails the hard pass.
